open_points.subject: flow:import_from_vps confirmation of a replaced upload
open_points.text: `capability:migration_import.confirm_import` refuses when the closure exists or the file of the bound digest is no longer kept
open_points.question: When the same bytes are uploaded again, must confirmation compare the bound upload number as well as the digest with the currently kept M21, which capability performs that check, and what refusal does a mismatch produce?
options: `confirm_import` compares both upload number and digest and refuses `file_not_kept` when either differs
replacing an upload clears any pending confirmation bound to the previous upload
the digest alone identifies the kept file, so re-uploading identical bytes permits the old confirmation
open_points.default_guess: Have `confirm_import` compare both the upload number and digest and refuse `file_not_kept` if either differs.

witness.initial: The migration closure is absent; one owner session keeps upload number 1 with bytes B and digest D, and has a pending clean confirmation bound to upload number 1, digest D and its mapping inputs.
events: The owner uploads B again in the same session; `keep_uploaded_file` replaces the kept value with upload number 2, still having digest D.
The owner submits the earlier confirmation form; `take_confirmation` consumes its still-matching pending value, then `confirm_import` examines the currently kept upload.
outcomes: Following “the file of the bound digest is no longer kept”, digest D is still kept, so the import may be accepted.
Following M21's upload-number identity and A16's same-bytes replacement rule, upload number 1 is no longer kept, so the import is refused as `file_not_kept`.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance versus refusal, and the store and audit log contain the imported records, closure and entry only in the first outcome.
